state.issue:
yq: =`'s right side still yields false for a zero-node literal/constructor operand (#2540 residual)

## Summary

[#2540](https://github.com/rust-works/succinctly/issues/2540) fixed `and`/`or`'s own read-only-context handling of a literal/constructor operand whose upstream pipe stage produced zero nodes (e.g. `(.a.zz | true) and true` now correctly answers `true`, matching real yq). The identical `Context.DontAutoCreate` mechanism (#2470) also applies to `=`'s right side, and it diverges the same way:

```console
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":true}
$ printf 'a:\n  b: 1\nx: 5\n' | succinctly yq -o=json -I0 '.x = (.a.zz | true)'
{"a":{"b":1},"x":5}
```

Real yq gives `x: true`; succinctly leaves `x` unchanged (`5`).

## Why #2540 didn't cover this

`and`/`or` evaluate their operands through `jq::eval::boolean_fanout_bools`, shared by both evaluators, which is where #2540's fix (`yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor`) was added. `=`'s right side evaluates through a completely separate mechanism (`jq::eval::yq_prepare_assign_targets`/`resolve_dynamic_indexes`), which #2540 did not touch — fixing this needs its own trace through that code path, not a second call to the same classifier from the wrong place.

## Suggested approach

Find wherever `=`'s right side currently registers "zero outputs" for the empty-context case (likely near `yq_prepare_assign_targets`'s own handling of a read-only right-side evaluation, #2470/#2481) and consult `jq::eval::yq_empty_context_literal_or_constructor` there the same way `boolean_fanout_bools` now does, before falling through to the existing "target unchanged" behavior.

## Verification notes

Re-verify the same shape matrix #2540 already established (literal, `[...]` — regardless of body, `{...}` — only when every field value also independently qualifies) against `=`'s right side specifically, since the surrounding mechanism differs even though the underlying "is this operand really empty" classification should be identical.

## Related

- #2540 (fixed `and`/`or`'s own copy of this gap)
- #2470 (the read-only context mechanism both share)
- `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`'s "An `and`/`or` operand's evaluation context" section, which already documents this residual
